| [LIT-140](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-140.md) v2 | Large Language Models Are Stochastic Measuring Devices | Mallory (2025), DOI-10.1093/9780191998317.003.0003. The chapter argues by analogy that deep neural networks are "stochastic measuring devices". Training alters the parameters in response to data, so that the resulting configuration carries information about the data ("training is measurement"). The trained weights are a model, and generation is simulation. DNNs are stochastic because random initialisation and non-convex loss mean runs need not converge to the same weights, failing Baird's "regularity" condition. The problems of interpreting model states and generated text are therefore the familiar problems of instruments, models and simulations. The problem of interpretable AI is an instance of the coordination problem in the philosophy of measurement. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-090](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-090.md)); worth reading as the most developed instrument-centred alternative to agentive framings of LLMs, and for its tidy division into model-interpretation, text-interpretation and linking problems; it offers an analogy, not a refutation (its own words, § Interpretation and Communication), and should be read in the published OUP version where possible. |

| [LIT-208](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-208.md) v2 | Distributional Semantics, Holism, and the Instability of Meaning | Grindrod et al. (2024), [ARXIV-2405.12084](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.12084). The authors argue that distributional models answer the instability objection to meaning holism if meaning is read "differentially", as a word's relations to its nearest neighbours, and not as its position in the space. They illustrate this with two corpus-expansion demonstrations. In a ±10-word count model on Stein's The Making of Americans (about 522k tokens), adding Hemingway's "A Clean, Well-Lighted Place" (under 1,500 words) shifts every cosine value for "know" by at most about 0.0005 (e.g. 0.95231 → 0.95284 for "understand") and leaves its top-10 neighbours in the same order, while "glass" gets a new neighbourhood. A Word2vec CBOW model on 143M words of Wikipedia shows the same pattern when about 21M words of the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (SEP) are added: "atomism" shifts, "can" barely moves. The residual instability, they argue, is a virtue. | Proposed — read in full 2026-09-26 (NOTE-158); promising as a philosophical reply, but its empirical half rests on top-10 neighbour tables for four hand-picked words, with no stability metric and no seed replication. Read it for its scope: the target is "strong AI", the claim that instantiating the right program is by itself sufficient for understanding, and Searle grants that machines, including artifacts with the brain's causal powers, could think. The argument is about understanding and intentionality; consciousness is mentioned, not argued. Its answer to the systems reply (internalise the room) is the part that bears on minds of parts, and it is asserted rather than shown: Searle says the subsystem is "simply a part of" the man, which is what the reply denies. |

It grants parity and argues that cognition has two necessary marks, non-derived content and a distinctive kind of causal process, which notebooks, screens and tools lack as a matter of contingent fact; and that brain-plus-tool systems are too motley to support a science. | [LIT-440](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-440.md) | Intentional Systems | Dennett (1971), Journal of Philosophy 68(4):87–106. An Intentional system is one whose behaviour can be explained and predicted by ascribing beliefs and desires and assuming rationality, which is the Intentional stance beside the design and physical stances. Being one is relative to an observer's strategy, and the choice of stance is pragmatic. The stance is "unmetaphysical": it sets aside composition, consciousness and moral standing. As psychology it is vacuous, because it presupposes rationality. Any theory that gives content to a part takes out a "loan of intelligence", repayable only by analysing away the part's reader: "there a little man is concealed". | Active — read in full 2026-10-02 ([NOTE-350](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-350.md)); worth reading as the first statement in print of the intentional stance and of the homunculus debt that Dennett later answers with "discharge". Its definition makes being an Intentional system relative to an observer's predictive strategy, and it says outright that the definition "does not say that Intentional systems really have beliefs and desires" (p. 91). True Believers ([LIT-398](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-398.md)) later withdraws exactly that relativity. Its lasting tool for this record is the "loan of intelligence" (p. 96): any theory that gives a part content owes an account of that part's reader, and "wherever a theory relies on a formulation bearing the logical marks of Intentionality, there a little man is concealed". The paper does not treat a group as an Intentional system. |
